These are constructed directory-backed metadata and real-file import fixtures.
Tests write actual METADATA/WHEEL/RECORD files, source/resources and optional real
CPython caches into a temporary installation tree. Standard library metadata,
PathFinder, source loaders, no-follow stream hashing and actual module/factory
sentinels exercise the capture/loading boundary. No capture engine is mocked.

The COLEMAN metadata catalogue is deliberately authored for isolated unit
mechanics over a complete byte copy of the actual SDK. The child imports that
copy, so its actual origin/resources and unchanged producer digest genuinely
join the declared directory image; no capture algorithm is mocked.
This is not the installed external Hedge qualification. That proof uses a fresh
noneditable wheel and the actual shared task service in the root qualification.

The approved tuple codec is a real frozen structural object, without a model
inheritance requirement. Loading must not call its `prepare` method. Negative
fixtures alter actual files/metadata, import search context or original approved
bindings and assert refusal before new provider/factory effects.
